descriptor: The tallest penguin, raising its chick on Antarctic sea ice through the darkest, coldest months.

range.summary: Circumpolar around the Antarctic coast, breeding in more than 60 known colonies on fast ice and foraging in the surrounding Southern Ocean.

population.unit: adult emperor penguins at colonies in spring (global satellite index)

source.label: LaRue et al. 2024, Proc. R. Soc. B 291: 20232067

population.note: The 2009 and 2018 values are stated in the paper; other years are read from its Figure 1 and are approximate to within about 2,000. This index counts adults present in late spring, so it is lower than the older 2009 estimate of about 238,000 breeding pairs.

threats.title: Early sea-ice break-up
threats.detail: When fast ice breaks up before chicks fledge, whole colonies can fail, as happened across the Bellingshausen Sea in 2022.

threats.title: Long-term sea-ice loss
threats.detail: Climate models project the global population will halve by the 2080s without deep emissions cuts.

threats.title: Moulting habitat loss
threats.detail: Adults need stable ice for a month each summer while they moult and cannot swim.

threats.title: Food web change
threats.detail: Shifts in sea ice alter the krill, fish and squid that emperors dive for.

source.label: IUCN Red List update: emperor penguin moved from Near Threatened to Endangered

places.name: Snow Hill Island
places.note: The most visited colony, reached by icebreaker and helicopter.

places.name: Gould Bay
places.note: Large colony reached by small-plane expeditions from Union Glacier.

places.name: Atka Bay
places.note: Colony near Germany's Neumayer station, visited on fly-in trips.

places.name: Pointe Geologie
places.note: Long-studied colony near Dumont d'Urville station, made famous on film.

places.name: Cape Washington
places.note: One of the largest colonies, occasionally reached by Ross Sea voyages.

sightings.tip: Late October to December, chicks have left their parents' feet and the fast ice still holds. Colonies disperse once the ice breaks up in summer.

actions.title: Cut your carbon emissions
actions.detail: Sea-ice loss driven by warming is the main threat, so emissions cuts matter more than anything else.

actions.title: Back Antarctic marine protected areas
actions.detail: Support proposals for protected areas in the Weddell Sea and East Antarctica at CCAMLR.

actions.title: Skip krill oil supplements
actions.detail: Antarctic krill fishing competes with penguins and their prey for the same food.

actions.title: Travel only with IAATO operators
actions.detail: Members follow distance and visitor limits that keep disturbance at colonies low.
